a.xlink:title: wallet Graph vertex: one row per Ethereum address. The hub nearly every other table references. (db/schema.sql)
block One row per Ethereum block a crawled transaction sits in. (db/schema.sql)

transaction Graph edge: a signed external transaction (associative entity resolving wallet-to-wallet m:n). (db/schema.sql) Indexes: idx_tx_from, idx_tx_to, idx_tx_block (schema.sql); idx_tx_to_block (to_wallet_id, block_number), idx_tx_from_block (from_wallet_id, block_number) and BRIN idx_tx_block_brin (block_number) (migration 002).
token One row per ERC-20 contract seen in a token transfer. (db/schema.sql)
token_transfer One row per ERC-20 Transfer event inside a transaction. (db/schema.sql)
label A named tag that can be attached to wallets (exchange, sanctioned, mixer...). (db/schema.sql)
wallet_label Associative entity: which labels apply to which wallet, and who applied them. (db/schema.sql)
analyst Who ran or reviewed an analysis. A seeded "system" row backs every pipeline run; distinct from app_user (sign-in). (db/schema.sql)
graph_snapshot A frozen, block-bounded edge list that every analysis run reads. (db/schema.sql)
snapshot_edge One aggregated wallet-to-wallet edge per snapshot (the CSR edge the graph algorithms consume). (db/schema.sql)
snapshot_edge_tx Bridge entity: traces one aggregated edge back to every transaction that fed it. (db/schema.sql)
algorithm Catalogue of runnable algorithms and detectors; seeded by schema.sql and migrations 003-004.
analysis_run One execution of one algorithm on one snapshot. Every result row below points back here. (db/schema.sql)
vertex_metric Per-wallet algorithm output (PageRank score, BFS distance...). (db/schema.sql)
cluster One Louvain community from one run. (db/schema.sql)
cluster_member Associative entity: which wallets belong to which cluster. (db/schema.sql)
alert A suspicious cluster or wallet raised for analyst review. (db/schema.sql)
visualization A rendered graph image produced from a run. (db/schema.sql)

framing_scenario One run of scripts/simulate_framing.py (simulation only, reversible with --cleanup). (migration 002) No FK by design: the attacker and target wallet ids are BIGINT[] arrays, which PostgreSQL cannot constrain with a foreign key.

flag One detector-raised signal that the audit engine interrogates for frameability. (migration 002) System-versioned (migration 009): trigger flag_versioning (AFTER UPDATE OR DELETE) writes every before-image into flag_history; flag_as_of(ts) and flag_versions(id) read it back.
flag_evidence The transactions a flag rests on, time-ordered by block. (migration 002)

flag_audit One audit verdict: could an outsider have manufactured this flag, and at what cost. (migration 002) Append-only and hash-chained (migration 009): trigger flag_audit_chain (BEFORE INSERT) links each row to the last; trigger flag_audit_append_only refuses UPDATE, and refuses DELETE unless framecheck.allow_audit_delete = on, tombstoning it. flag_audit_chain_verify() names the first row that does not fit.

flag_history Before-images of every changed or deleted flag, with the period each version was valid for. Written only by trigger flag_versioning. (migration 009) No FK by design: history must outlive the flag it describes -- scripts/run_experiment.py deletes flags wholesale, and a FK would block that or cascade the history away. Non-overlap: EXCLUDE USING gist (flag_id WITH =, sys_period WITH &&) as flag_history_no_overlap when btree_gist is available, else a unique index on (flag_id, lower(sys_period)).

flag_audit_tombstone Every audit row ever deleted, who deleted it and why. A chain gap with no tombstone is tampering; a gap with one is housekeeping. Written only by trigger flag_audit_append_only. (migration 009) No FK by design: it names flag_audit rows that have been deleted, so there is nothing left to reference.

app_user A person who signed in with Google. (migration 006) No FK by design: "Nothing in the analysis schema references this table: the audit trail is about wallets, not operators, and FrameCheck must keep working with auth disabled."
schema_migration Which migration files have been applied to this database. Created by api/dbsetup.py, not by a migration. No FK by design: bookkeeping about the schema itself, not data in it.
